name: Seated Cable Row — Wide Lat Bar
description: The seated cable row with a wide lat bar uses a pronated (overhand) wide grip, shifting emphasis from the lower lats and biceps toward the rhomboids, middle trapezius, and rear deltoids compared to a neutral-grip V-bar row. The wider grip requires greater horizontal shoulder abduction and places the shoulder in a position that more directly targets the upper back retractors. It is an effective mid-back mass builder.

execution.starting_position: Attach a wide lat bar to the seated cable row machine. Sit with feet on footrests, knees slightly bent. Grip the bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder width.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the seat so the cable is at chest height when seated. Sit tall with a neutral spine before initiating each rep.
steps: Step 1: Sit with the arms extended toward the cable, gripping the wide bar overhand.
Step 2: Begin from a slight forward lean with the shoulder blades protracted.
Step 3: Row the bar toward the lower sternum by retracting the scapulae and driving the elbows out and back.
Step 4: Squeeze the mid-back hard at peak contraction.
Step 5: Return under control to the starting extended position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Rocking the torso back excessively instead of using the back muscles
Not fully protracting the scapulae at the start of each rep
Pulling the bar to the abdomen — target is the lower sternum with this grip width
safety_considerations: The wider grip places the shoulder in greater external rotation — do not force range of motion if discomfort is felt
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full scapular protraction at the start, full retraction at the end of each rep.
coaching_cues: Let the shoulder blades spread at the start
Squeeze the mid-back — not just the lats
